newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wage growth may prompt Australian rate hike - OECD.
newsitem.headline: Wage growth may prompt Australian rate hike - OECD.

text.p: Wage growth could trigger interest rate rises to combat inflation in Australia during the coming year, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Friday.
Inflation targets would be threatened if recent five-percent wages growth in enterprise agreements -- the term for employment contracts -- continued and spread more widely, the OECD said.

"This would necessitate a tightening in monetary policy, resulting in a weaker outlook for growth and unemployment," it said. The report was written after the Reserve Bank's July and November rate cuts but preceded a third in mid-December which took overnight cash rates down to 6.0 percent.
Annual enterprise-agreement wage inflation dropped to 4.8 percent in the September quarter from 5.3 percent in the previous quarter.
"(Gross Domestic Product) growth is projected to slow to about three percent by 1998, and the composition of domestic demand is likely to shift towards capital formation," the OECD said.
The government projects consistent economic growth of between 3.25 to 3.5 percent until mid-2000, compared with the 3.8 percent growth recorded between the September quarters of 1995 and 1996.
"Employment growth may pick up gradually, from 1.25 percent in 1996 to around 1.75 percent in 1997-98," the OECD said.
"With rising labour force participation, this will probably reduce unemployment by only a little, to around eight percent in 1998."
Government fiscal projections assume employment growth of 1.25 percent in the fiscal year to June 1997 and 2.0 to 2.25 percent in the three following years.
The government forecasts 8.25 percent unemployment in the June quarter of 1997 but has not issued a more distant projection.
